Subject: Reranking follow-up + recommended next steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary from call
- Primary goal: improve ordering for search results on product pages; KPI = add-to-cart rate and checkout conversion.
- Current infra: proprietary BM25 + small neural re-ranker running on CPU; latency budget ~120ms P95.
- Data: historical clicks + add-to-cart logs (6 months), labeled relevance for ~8k queries.

Initial model fit recommendation
- Shortlist: a distil cross-encoder quantized (4-bit) for rerank + lightweight learned scoring head for final score.
- Why: proven MRR/NDCG gains in similar merchants while staying within latency when colocated on a g4-like instance and using prefix caching.

What we’ll deliver as next actions
1) Redwood will run an offline fit eval and return NDCG@10 and MRR by query bucket. We’ll include prompt sets and the eval harness. (Target by EOD tomorrow)
2) If fit looks good, we propose a 2-week A/B canary (10% traffic) with automatic fallback. We’ll provide suggested experiment metrics and slicing.
3) Procurement/contract: Nate said procurement will need a short MSA addendum for data retention — I’ll loop your procurement contact.

Attachments: I’m including a compact eval plan and the prompt set we’ll use for human inspection.

Can you confirm:
- A sample export with the labeled queries + impressions that we discussed can be shared to the Drive link?
- Who on your side will own the canary monitoring (alerts to on-call or CS)?

Thanks — I’ll kick off the offline runs once you confirm access.

Camila Reyes

Subject: Re: Reranking fit eval results (NDCG/MRR) + A/B proposal

Team / Alex — posting the offline fit results from the run we kicked off after the call. Summary first, details below. Attachment: fathom-ndcg-mrr-summary.csv

Executive summary
- Variant A (distil-cross-encoder, 4-bit quantized): NDCG@10 = 0.621 (+14% vs baseline), MRR = 0.482 (+18%).
- Variant B (float cross-encoder w/ calibrated head): NDCG@10 = 0.635 (+17%), MRR = 0.498 (+21%).
- Latency (simulated per-request with KV cache hit rate ~35%, seq len 60): A P95 = 98ms, B P95 = 160ms.

Interpretation
- Both variants materially improve quality vs your current re-ranker. Variant B is stronger quality-wise but exceeds your 120ms P95 budget in our synthetic sim. Variant A meets latency but with slightly lower quality.

Recommended A/B plan for production validation
- Canary length: 14 days, allocation: 10% traffic (5% A, 5% B), holdout = 90% baseline.
- Primary metrics: add-to-cart rate (aggregate + per-query-slice), NDCG@10 on labelled queries, checkout conversion delta.
- Safety nets: automatic rollback if add-to-cart drops >1.5% absolute for >30 minutes or if P95 > 200ms for >10 minutes.
- Analysis slices: brand queries, category navigational, long-tail (queries <5 occurrences), device mobile vs desktop.

Benchmark artifacts and links
- Full CSV: https://drive.google.com/file/d/fathom-ndcg-mrr-summary.csv
- Eval harness & prompt-set: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cFathomBenchmarks (includes prompt-set-v2.json used for human checks).

Notes on quality regression risk
- We observed a small cluster of queries where Variant B reorders a correct result below the previous top-3 (~0.6% of eval queries). We’ve added those to a regression watchlist included in the prompt-set for manual triage.
- Suggest a smoke-run in staging with a sample of live queries prior to canary. That will surface infra edge cases and cold-cache behavior.

Attachments: fathom-ndcg-mrr-summary.csv (perf/metrics), prompt-set-v2.json (human inspect prompts)

Let me know if you want me to draft the experiment config (traffic split, flags) and the rollback playbook — happy to push a PR to your Ops repo.

— Aditya
